subject: Request: Clearance for performance-benchmark & MFN ask from Bryton Health
participants_external: Mark Reeves (mark.reeves@brytonhealth.com) - Bryton Health, Head of Procurement
body:
---Message 1 (oldest)---
From: Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@brytonhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@brytonhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOW + key contract asks (MFN + benchmark clause)

Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with latency and the token-cost breakdown. We reviewed SOW_v3 and the pricing spreadsheet (attached). Legal has two high-level commercial asks before we proceed to signature:

1) We need an MFN-style clause that ensures Bryton will receive pricing no worse than any direct competitors for a comparable workload for the first 18 months.
2) We want a clause that allows Bryton to benchmark Redwood performance against a named competitive index quarterly; if Redwood misses the benchmark in two consecutive quarters, Bryton can request remediation credits or rate adjustments.

We also expect a modest exclusivity carveout that limits Redwood from selling a specific integrated healthcare search feature to other mid-market digital health customers in the US for 18 months.

I know these are material asks — can you confirm whether Redwood would accept MFN + the benchmark mechanism and a limited exclusivity term in exchange for the 25% first-year committed-capacity discount we discussed?

Attached: Bryton_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), Pricing_Comparison.xlsx

—Mark
Head of Procurement, Bryton Health

---Message 2---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SOW + key contract asks (MFN + benchmark clause) — escalation/exec review needed

Laura / Tessa — forwarding Bryton's asks. TL;DR: MFN for 18 months, quarterly benchmark + remediation credits, and an 18-month product-level exclusivity carveout. They are offering a 25% committed-capacity discount in return.

Why this is risky: MFN scope is broad ("comparable workload") and open-ended. Benchmark language gives them a remedy if our runtime underperforms compared to public competitors (could trigger credits or price reduction). Exclusivity on a product feature in our target vertical is commercially sensitive.

Proposed negotiation positions (draft):
- MFN: limit to identical contractual terms (list to be defined), timebox to 12 months, exclude promotional/partner deals, and cap refunds/credits to a $ value tied to committed spend.
- Benchmark: agree to objective test harness (we propose Redwood-supplied benchmark harness + third-party observer), limit remediation to engineering remediation plan + service credits capped at one monthly committed fee, not an automatic price reset.
- Exclusivity: convert to a non-solicit/priority-support pledge for Bryton in specified geos for 12 months, not categorical prohibition; or convert to first-refusal on product roadmap items with sunset.

Asking for executive clearance to sign down to: MFN (12 months, narrowly scoped), Benchmark (third-party observed, limited credits), Exclusivity (priority/first-refusal, 12 months) in exchange for the 25% first-year committed capacity discount.

Can you confirm whether we should approve that tradeoff or need to escalate to legal + celo execs? I can draft redlines if you want.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---Message 3---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOW + key contract asks (MFN + benchmark clause) — proposed guardrails

Aditya — good summary. My quick take: we should aim to keep the MFN commercially narrow and avoid any retroactive price adjustments. Specific suggestions for redlines:

- MFN: "Redwood will offer pricing and commercial terms no less favorable than those extended to customers of equivalent scale and use. MFN shall apply for 12 months from Effective Date and shall exclude promotional pricing, partner channel pricing, and any government/volume-based tenders."
- Benchmark: require a jointly-approved benchmark harness that runs on a mutually agreed test set, limit measurement to P95 latency and token-efficiency for identical prompt sets, and cap remedies to service credits not exceeding 10% of monthly committed fees for the quarter in which the failure occurs. No automatic price reduction.
- Exclusivity: convert to a commercial 'no direct competitive go-to-market' clause limited to the exact feature set described in SOW Section 2.1, duration 12 months, and exclude public cloud marketplace transactions and broad OEM channels.

If we get buy-in from Sales + Legal on these redlines I would be comfortable approving at manager level. Anything beyond (18 months or uncapped credits) should go to CRO/CEO for approval.

Laura
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

---Message 4---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@brytonhealth.com>, contracts@brytonhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOW + key contract asks (MFN + benchmark clause)

Mark — thanks for the clarity and the attachments. We appreciate the constructive posture.

We can move forward with a compromise that protects Bryton's economics while keeping Redwood's commercial safeguards intact. High-level counterproposals (will follow formal redline):

1) MFN: We can agree to an MFN limited to materially identical commercial terms for comparable workload and purchaser scale, time-limited to 12 months from Effective Date. MFN will exclude: promotional offers, channel/partner pricing, and government/tender awards. Any price adjustments under MFN will be prospective and subject to a maximum annual adjustment cap equal to 5% of the then-current per-unit price.

2) Benchmark: We will accept a quarterly benchmark review using a jointly-approved harness and an independent observer. Remedies for missing the benchmark will be limited to a corrective action plan plus service credits capped at 10% of the monthly committed fee for that quarter. No automatic price resets or retroactive refunds.

3) Exclusivity: We cannot accept a broad product exclusivity. We will offer a 12-month priority roadmap commitment for the feature in Section 2.1 of the SOW and a right-of-first-refusal on equivalent product integrations. This will exclude public marketplace listings and broad OEM agreements.

In return we will hold the 25% committed-capacity discount for Year 1 and prioritize onboarding timeframes.

If this is acceptable, please confirm and we will circulate formal redlines and route the SOW through DocuSign.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed redline to follow (Bryton_SOW_v3 - referenced)

---Message 5 (most recent)---
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOW + key contract asks (MFN + benchmark clause) — exec clearance granted at manager level

Aditya / Laura — I reviewed the counterpoints. Manager-level signoff: APPROVED to proceed with the proposed redlines (MFN 12 months narrow scope; benchmark with independent observer and capped credits; exclusivity converted to priority/ROFR for 12 months).

Please ensure Legal runs final redlines and includes: an explicit test harness appendix, a cap on cumulative credits across the term, and a mutual termination row for persistent breaches limited to engineered remediation timelines. If any party pushes for 18-month MFN or uncapped credits, escalate immediately to CRO.

Tessa Morgan
VP Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
